sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A compact agave of coastal and dry-scrub habitats in southern California and Baja California. Its thick green leaves have hooked marginal teeth and a dark terminal spine; rosettes can reach about 1 m across. Flower stalks rise several metres and bear yellowish flowers. Each rosette dies after flowering, though offsets may persist.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: An ethnobotanical source reports traditional nectar collection from A. shawii. This does not establish general food use of all plant parts.
